**DELIBERATE CORRECTION** of `.changeset/34648-skills-result-dialog-bulk-result.md`, the only foreign note edited. `Check Changeset` is red by design, and the declaration is in the body under `## DELIBERATE CORRECTION`. - Before: "A second entry teaches what an `execution: 'aggregate'` bulk handler resolves with when it wrote some rows and refused others, `{ succeeded: string[], failed: [{ id, message }] }`, that it resolves and does not throw, and how the console counts the ids. One eval case for each."

The corrected sentence is true, and the two notes no longer contradict each other in one changelog. The title line ("…teaches … the aggregate bulk handler's `BulkActionResult`") is left as it was, and it is still true in substance: the rule still teaches that type, by its reading. Not blocking.

The new "not `execution: 'perRecord'` added while the `bulkActionDefs` aggregate entry stays" line closes the half-migration answer.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `31062c7b2dd1d05aaae854fb023f2355a680bca5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-ui/evals/views-apps-actions-pages.json, skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md + none
Security-touching: yes

PR #36418, card #36156. Net diff against `main` (merge base `4e55e4eb`, `main` read at `761220c6`): 4 files, 18 added, 5 deleted. The two `hits` files and the 34648 note are unchanged on `main` since the merge base. No file in the diff implements or enforces the `hits` files, so the scope adds none. The two changesets are the lane seat's remainder. They are read here only for ② and for the correction this record is asked to confirm.

`Security-touching: yes` is meant. The changed bullet teaches read-scope behaviour: which selected ids reach a body, and that one id the caller cannot read refuses the call with 404. The seat adopting this record adds the `security` label.

### ① Derived judgments

- Public surface: one bullet of the published `objectstack-ui` actions rule, and eval case 23 of `views-apps-actions-pages.json`. No schema, no accept set, no code. Right.
- The rule stops teaching an aggregate handler that writes rows one by one and resolves with a `succeeded` / `failed` pair, and teaches `execution: 'perRecord'` for that body. This is what the card asks for and what `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx` says on `main` ("A body that writes each selected row is best declared `execution: 'perRecord'`"). Right.
- The spec still lets an aggregate handler resolve with a `BulkActionResult` (`bulk-action.zod.ts`, "MAY resolve with"). The skill now steers away from it and keeps only the reading rule. That narrows the teaching, not the runtime. Right, and it is the card's stated intent.
- Case 23 has a new token set, so a new hash. Earlier recordings of the case are set apart on a regrade. Right, and the PR's own note says so.
- Gates on this head: every check-run is `success` or an expected skip, except `Check Changeset`, which is `failure` on both of its runs. Job 137195709607: "Require a changeset" is `success`; the one failed step is "Reject an empty-frontmatter changeset added by this PR", and its one error names `.changeset/34648-skills-result-dialog-bulk-result.md` as a note that exists on the merge base. Nothing else is red. So the check is red only for the edited pending note, which is the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class, by design. The PR carries no `skip-changeset` label. Right.
- Token ratchet: the rule file is reported at 3710 of 3711. The gates that enforce it are green on this head.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/36156-actions-per-record-write.md` bumps `@objectstack/skills` by `patch`. The diff changes skill text and an eval fixture only. Patch is the right level.
- `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are on the PR body and on the new note. The diff removes no declared capability from a consumer, so `no` is right.
- Each sentence of the new note agrees with the diff at this head, including the two forbidden tokens and the "script body or a flow" wording.
- DELIBERATE CORRECTION of `.changeset/34648-skills-result-dialog-bulk-result.md`: confirmed. The PR body declares it and quotes the sentence before and after, and the quotation matches the diff. The old sentence said a second entry teaches what an aggregate handler resolves with, that it resolves and does not throw, how the console counts the ids, and "One eval case for each". This PR removes all of that from the rule and moves the only bulk-result eval case to the per-record form, so the old sentence would be false in the same release. The new sentence says the entry tells how an aggregate return value is read, and "One eval case for `resultDialog`" (case 22). Both are true at this head. Front matter and declaration lines are untouched.
- The title line of 34648 still reads "teaches ... the aggregate bulk handler's `BulkActionResult`". I do not read the release text as contradicting itself. The rule still names `BulkActionResult` with its import path and still says how it is read, the 34648 body now says exactly that, and the 36156 note says what was dropped and "What stays of `BulkActionResult`". The title is looser than the body, not opposed to it. Nit N2 below.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in both dev reports. Nothing to escalate.
- Dev flag, `BulkActionResult` kept as one reading clause: accepted. The clause is true on `main` (`readAggregateResult` in `ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/hooks/useBulkExecutor.ts`), and it still protects an aggregate body that returns counts. Do not drop it.
- Dev flag, no separate replacement wording existed for the card: accepted. PR #36132 and PR #36067 are both merged, and the wording agrees with `actions.mdx` on `main`.
- Dev flag, `list_toolbar` row left unchanged: accepted. It is outside the diff and not reviewed.
- Dev flag, `Check Changeset` red with no `skip-changeset` label: accepted, see ① and ②.
- Dev flag, overlap-check exit 1 against the bot's version-packages PR 35129 alone: accepted. That PR deletes every pending note. It is a landing-order matter for the seat, not a defect of this diff.
- Dev flag, the PR body was written by the seat, not the dev: the body on GitHub now carries the round-2 text and the DELIBERATE CORRECTION section. Answered.
- Dev flag, the first commit keeps a `wip:` subject: accepted, the PR title carries the conventional one.
- Dev flag, one derived gate not measured locally: the check-runs on the head are the verdict, and they are green.
- Dev note that `views.mdx` and the `bulkActionDefs` description in `view.zod.ts` still describe an aggregate handler answering with a `BulkActionResult`: true of the runtime, outside the card. Not escalated.
- SQL push-down: the diff holds no code, no id materialisation and no join. Nothing to flag.
- No security finding. `security_findings` is `none` in both reports and I found none.

### ④ Design judgment

**`skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md`**, the one changed bullet, sentence by sentence against `main`:

1. "A list view's `bulkActions: ['NAME']` runs the action once per ticked row." Holds. `actions.mdx` table, and the `execution` describe text in `action.zod.ts`.
2. "A body that writes each selected row takes that form: declare `execution: 'perRecord'` and write the row it is handed (`ctx.record`, `ctx.recordId`; `crm_create_campaign` below)." Holds. `BulkActionExecutionSchema` is `perRecord` or `aggregate`. The example below the bullet declares `execution: 'perRecord'` and writes with `ctx.recordId`. I tried the other per-record spelling, a `bulkActionDefs` entry with `operation: 'custom'` and no `aggregate`: the spec refuses it and names `bulkActions` as the per-record form, so the sentence names the only valid wiring.
3. "a row whose run throws is listed with its message." Holds. The per-row path in `useBulkExecutor.ts` settles a rejected row as failed and pushes its id and error.
4. "A `bulkActionDefs` entry `{ name, operation: 'custom', execution: 'aggregate' }` runs it once for the selection." Holds, and the spec requires `aggregate` on a custom def.
5. "A script body or a flow receives the ids under the built-in key `params._selectedIds` (`input._selectedIds`), at most 5000 and only ids the caller can read: one the caller cannot read refuses the whole call (`404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND`) before it starts." Holds. `actionSelectionIsRead` in `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts` reads every arm but the declarative update, a `type: 'api'` action and the system principal, so "a script body or a flow" is exactly the read set. `ACTION_SELECTION_CAP` is 5000. `loadActionSelectionRecords` reads every distinct id with the per-record door's own caller-scope read and drops none. `refuseUndeliveredActionSelection` throws the record-not-found refusal in `dispatchAdmittedAction` ahead of the flow and script arms. I tried to break it with an `api` action, a declarative update and a registered handler: the first two are outside the sentence's subject, and a registered handler is a script arm and is read. The sentence does not overclaim.
6. "A throw is one outcome for the selection; a return value with a top-level `succeeded` or `failed` is read as a `BulkActionResult` (`@objectstack/spec/ui`), any other form (counts, one list) reported as unreadable." Holds as meant. `readAggregateResult` returns `unreadable` only when one of the two members is present and the value does not parse. See N1.

Against the card: the per-record form is taught, the aggregate facts are stated (key, cap, caller scope), and no example or sentence in the file writes rows from an aggregate selection any more. The card's owed items for this file are met.

**`skills/objectstack-ui/evals/views-apps-actions-pages.json`**, case 23:

- The prompt is unchanged. The expected answer agrees with the rule and with the spec, and it names the half-done answer as wrong. It carries all three required tokens and neither forbidden one.
- Grading is literal, case-sensitive substring matching (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`, "Grading").
- Half-done answer, `perRecord` added while the aggregate `bulkActionDefs` entry stays: it lacks `bulkActions: [`, because `bulkActionDefs: [` does not contain that string. It fails. Good. The linter would also refuse that app (`action-dispatch-contract-mismatch`), so failing it is right.
- Aggregate loop that returns the pair: it lacks the required tokens, and `succeeded:` or `succeeded,` catches the mixed forms. Good.

S1 (should-fix) — the forbidden token `succeeded,` is ordinary English. A correct per-record answer that describes the dialog in prose, for example "rows that succeeded, and each locked row with its message", fails the case. The prompt asks the answer to explain what the dialog will say, so this wording is likely. The dev report shows the same effect from the other side: the reference answer had to be reworded so it would not trip the token. Use a token that prose cannot hit and that still covers the shorthand return, for example `{ succeeded` in place of `succeeded,`. Together with `succeeded:` it catches the shorthand, the single-line keyed form and the multi-line keyed form.

Nits, no effect on the verdict:

- N1, rule sentence 6: "any other form" can be read as "any other return value", which would be false. A value with neither member keeps the one-outcome report. The examples in brackets point to the right reading, and the 36156 note already says "any other form of those members". If a token can be found, say "of them" in the rule too.
- N2, the 34648 title line: looser than its corrected body, as said in ②. Accepted as is. A title edit is optional and belongs to the same declared correction.
- N3, case 23: `bulkActions: [` misses a JSON-quoted answer (`"bulkActions": [`), and a reversed shorthand (`{ failed, succeeded }`) escapes both forbidden tokens. The second matters little, since such an answer also has to carry all three required tokens.

No must-fix. One should-fix, S1, open on this head.
